v: How[^1] lonely sits the city that was full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations. The princess among the provinces has been put to forced labor.
אֵיכָ֣ה ׀ יָשְׁבָ֣ה בָדָ֗ד הָעִיר֙ רַבָּ֣תִי עָ֔ם הָיְתָ֖ה כְּאַלְמָנָ֑ה רַּבָּ֣תִי בַגּוֹיִ֗ם שָׂרָ֙תִי֙ בַּמְּדִינ֔וֹת הָיְתָ֖ה לָמַֽס׃ ס
She weeps bitterly in the night, with tears on her cheeks. Among all her lovers she has no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
בָּכ֨וֹ תִבְכֶּ֜ה בַּלַּ֗יְלָה וְדִמְעָתָהּ֙ עַ֣ל לֶֽחֱיָ֔הּ אֵֽין־לָ֥הּ מְנַחֵ֖ם מִכָּל־אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ כָּל־רֵעֶ֙יהָ֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔הּ הָ֥יוּ לָ֖הּ לְאֹיְבִֽים׃ ס
Judah has gone into exile after affliction and harsh servitude.[^2] She lives among the nations, but finds no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the narrow places.[^3]
גָּֽלְתָ֨ה יְהוּדָ֤ה מֵעֹ֙נִי֙ וּמֵרֹ֣ב עֲבֹדָ֔ה הִ֚יא יָשְׁבָ֣ה בַגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א מָצְאָ֖ה מָנ֑וֹחַ כָּל־רֹדְפֶ֥יהָ הִשִּׂיג֖וּהָ בֵּ֥ין הַמְּצָרִֽים׃ ס
The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to the festivals. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan; her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitterness.
דַּרְכֵ֨י צִיּ֜וֹן אֲבֵל֗וֹת מִבְּלִי֙ בָּאֵ֣י מוֹעֵ֔ד כָּל־שְׁעָרֶ֙יהָ֙ שֽׁוֹמֵמִ֔ין כֹּהֲנֶ֖יהָ נֶאֱנָחִ֑ים בְּתוּלֹתֶ֥יהָ נּ[t]וּג֖וֹת וְהִ֥יא מַר־לָֽהּ׃ ס
Her foes have become her masters;[^4] her enemies are at ease. For the LORD[^5] has made her suffer for her many rebellions. Her little children have gone into captivity before the foe.
הָי֨וּ צָרֶ֤יהָ לְרֹאשׁ֙ אֹיְבֶ֣יהָ שָׁל֔וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה הוֹגָ֖הּ עַ֣ל רֹב־פְּשָׁעֶ֑יהָ עוֹלָלֶ֛יהָ הָלְכ֥וּ שְׁבִ֖י לִפְנֵי־צָֽר׃ ס
All her splendor has departed from Daughter Zion.[^6] Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they have gone on without strength before the pursuer.
וַיֵּצֵ֥א *מן *בת־**מִבַּת־צִיּ֖וֹן כָּל־הֲדָרָ֑הּ הָי֣וּ שָׂרֶ֗יהָ כְּאַיָּלִים֙ לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מִרְעֶ֔ה וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְלֹא־כֹ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י רוֹדֵֽף׃ ס

In the days of her affliction and her homelessness, Jerusalem remembers all the precious things that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the hand of the foe, and there was no one to help her, the foes looked at her; they laughed at her ruin.[^7]

זָֽכְרָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם יְמֵ֤י עָנְיָהּ֙ וּמְרוּדֶ֔יהָ כֹּ֚ל מַחֲמֻדֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מִ֣ימֵי קֶ֑דֶם בִּנְפֹ֧ל עַמָּ֣הּ בְּיַד־צָ֗ר וְאֵ֤ין עוֹזֵר֙ לָ֔הּ רָא֣וּהָ צָרִ֔ים שָׂחֲק֖וּ עַ֥ל מִשְׁבַּתֶּֽהָ׃ ס
Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become a thing to scorn.[^8] All who honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away.
חֵ֤טְא חָֽטְאָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן לְנִידָ֣ה הָיָ֑תָה כָּֽל־מְכַבְּדֶ֤יהָ הִזִּיל֙וּהָ֙ כִּי־רָא֣וּ עֶרְוָתָ֔הּ גַּם־הִ֥יא נֶאֶנְחָ֖ה וַתָּ֥שָׁב אָחֽוֹר׃ ס
Her uncleanness is in her skirts; she did not consider her end. Her fall was astonishing; there is no one to comfort her. Look, LORD, at my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed![^9]
טֻמְאָתָ֣הּ בְּשׁוּלֶ֗יהָ לֹ֤א זָֽכְרָה֙ אַחֲרִיתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד פְּלָאִ֔ים אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י הִגְדִּ֖יל אוֹיֵֽב׃ ס
The foe has stretched out his hand over all her precious things; for she has seen the nations enter her sanctuary, those you commanded not to enter your assembly.[^10]
יָדוֹ֙ פָּ֣רַשׂ צָ֔ר עַ֖ל כָּל־מַחֲמַדֶּ֑יהָ כִּֽי־רָאֲתָ֤ה גוֹיִם֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִקְדָּשָׁ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֔יתָה לֹא־יָבֹ֥אוּ בַקָּהָ֖ל לָֽךְ׃ ס
All her people groan as they search for bread; they give their treasures for food to keep themselves alive.[^11] Look, LORD, and see, for I am despised.
כָּל־עַמָּ֤הּ נֶאֱנָחִים֙ מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם נָתְנ֧וּ *מחמו[y]*דיהם **מַחֲמַדֵּיהֶ֛ם בְּאֹ֖כֶל לְהָשִׁ֣יב נָ֑פֶשׁ רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה כִּ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה׃ ס
Is it nothing to you,[^12] all you who pass by on the road? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, which was dealt out to me, which the LORD inflicted on the day of his burning anger.
ל֣וֹא אֲלֵיכֶם֮ כָּל־עֹ֣בְרֵי דֶרֶךְ֒ הַבִּ֣יטוּ וּרְא֔וּ אִם־יֵ֤שׁ מַכְאוֹב֙ כְּמַכְאֹבִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עוֹלַ֖ל לִ֑י אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹגָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בְּי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃ ס
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overcame them.[^13] He spread a net for my feet; he turned me back. He has made me desolate, sick all day long.
מִמָּר֛וֹם שָֽׁלַח־אֵ֥שׁ בְּעַצְמֹתַ֖י וַיִּרְדֶּ֑נָּה פָּרַ֨שׂ רֶ֤שֶׁת לְרַגְלַי֙ הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי אָח֔וֹר נְתָנַ֙נִי֙ שֹֽׁמֵמָ֔ה כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם דָּוָֽה׃ ס

The yoke of my rebellions has been bound on;[^14] by his hand they were woven together. They have come up on my neck; he has made my strength fail. The Lord has given me into the hands of those I cannot withstand.
נִשְׂקַד֩ עֹ֨ל פְּשָׁעַ֜י בְּיָד֗וֹ יִשְׂתָּֽרְג֛וּ עָל֥וּ עַל־צַוָּארִ֖י הִכְשִׁ֣יל כֹּחִ֑י נְתָנַ֣נִי אֲדֹנָ֔י בִּידֵ֖י לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל קֽוּם׃ ס
The Lord has rejected[^15] all my mighty men in my midst; he has called an assembly[^16] against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden Virgin Daughter Judah as in a winepress.[^17]
סִלָּ֨ה כָל־אַבִּירַ֤י ׀ אֲדֹנָי֙ בְּקִרְבִּ֔י קָרָ֥א עָלַ֛י מוֹעֵ֖ד לִשְׁבֹּ֣ר בַּחוּרָ֑י גַּ֚ת דָּרַ֣ךְ אֲדֹנָ֔י לִבְתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־יְהוּדָֽה׃ ס
For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, for a comforter is far from me, one to revive my soul. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.
עַל־אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ אֲנִ֣י בוֹכִיָּ֗ה עֵינִ֤י ׀ עֵינִי֙ יֹ֣רְדָה מַּ֔יִם כִּֽי־רָחַ֥ק מִמֶּ֛נִּי מְנַחֵ֖ם מֵשִׁ֣יב נַפְשִׁ֑י הָי֤וּ בָנַי֙ שֽׁוֹמֵמִ֔ים כִּ֥י גָבַ֖ר אוֹיֵֽב׃ ס

Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her.[^18] The LORD has commanded against Jacob that his neighbors should be his foes. Jerusalem has become an unclean thing[^19] among them.
פֵּֽרְשָׂ֨ה צִיּ֜וֹן בְּיָדֶ֗יהָ אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לָ֔הּ צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב סְבִיבָ֣יו צָרָ֑יו הָיְתָ֧ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם לְנִדָּ֖ה בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃ ס
The LORD is in the right, for I rebelled against his word.[^20] Hear now, all peoples, and see my pain! My young women and my young men have gone into captivity.
צַדִּ֥יק ה֛וּא יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י פִ֣יהוּ מָרִ֑יתִי שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א כָל־*עמים **הָֽעַמִּ֗ים וּרְאוּ֙ מַכְאֹבִ֔י בְּתוּלֹתַ֥י וּבַחוּרַ֖י הָלְכ֥וּ בַשֶּֽׁבִי׃ ס
I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city as they searched for food to keep themselves alive.[^21]
קָרָ֤אתִי לַֽמְאַהֲבַי֙ הֵ֣מָּה רִמּ֔וּנִי כֹּהֲנַ֥י וּזְקֵנַ֖י בָּעִ֣יר גָּוָ֑עוּ כִּֽי־בִקְשׁ֥וּ אֹ֙כֶל֙ לָ֔מוֹ וְיָשִׁ֖יבוּ אֶת־נַפְשָֽׁם׃ ס
Look, LORD, for I am in distress! My insides churn; my heart is overturned within me, for I have been very rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.[^22]
רְאֵ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה כִּֽי־צַר־לִי֙ מֵעַ֣י חֳמַרְמָ֔רוּ נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ לִבִּי֙ בְּקִרְבִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָר֖וֹ מָרִ֑יתִי מִח֥וּץ שִׁכְּלָה־חֶ֖רֶב בַּבַּ֥יִת כַּמָּֽוֶת׃ ס

They have heard that I groan; there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they rejoice that you have done it. Bring on the day you have announced,[^23] and let them become like me.
שָׁמְע֞וּ כִּ֧י נֶאֱנָחָ֣ה אָ֗נִי אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י כָּל־אֹ֨יְבַ֜י שָׁמְע֤וּ רָֽעָתִי֙ שָׂ֔שׂוּ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ הֵבֵ֥אתָ יוֹם־קָרָ֖אתָ וְיִֽהְי֥וּ כָמֽוֹנִי׃ ס
Let all their evil come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my rebellions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.
תָּבֹ֨א כָל־רָעָתָ֤ם לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ וְעוֹלֵ֣ל לָ֔מוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עוֹלַ֛לְתָּ לִ֖י עַ֣ל כָּל־פְּשָׁעָ֑י כִּֽי־רַבּ֥וֹת אַנְחֹתַ֖י וְלִבִּ֥י דַוָּֽי׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *eikhah*, "How!", a cry of lament (compare 2 Samuel 1:19), which gives the book its Hebrew name. Chapters 1–4 are acrostic poems. In this chapter the twenty-two verses begin with the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, from *alef* to *tav*. Each verse has three lines, except verse 7, which has four.
n.2: Or "because of affliction and harsh servitude".
n.3: Or "in the midst of her distress".
n.4: Literally "have become the head". Compare Deuteronomy 28:44.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Hebrew *bat-tsiyyon*, a poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman.
n.7: Hebrew *mishbatteha*, a word found only here, perhaps "her ruin" or "her ceasing".
n.8: Hebrew *nidah*, a word found only here. It may mean "an object of scorn" (from *nud*, "to shake the head"), or it may be another form of *niddah*, "unclean thing" (verse 17).
n.9: Jerusalem herself speaks in this line, in the last line of verse 11, and in verses 12–16 and 18–22. The poem does not mark where her words begin and end, so they are not put in quotation marks.
n.11: Literally "to bring back life (*nephesh*)". Also in verse 19.
n.12: Literally "Not to you". The meaning is uncertain: perhaps "May it not happen to you".
n.14: Hebrew *nisqad*, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning.
n.16: Hebrew *mo'ed*, an appointed time or festival, as in verse 4.
n.17: Literally "A winepress the Lord has trodden for the virgin, Daughter Judah".
n.18: The poet speaks in this verse.
n.19: Hebrew *niddah*, the uncleanness of a woman during her monthly period (Leviticus 15:19–24).
n.21: The Septuagint adds "but they found none".
n.22: Literally "in the house, it is like death".
n.23: Literally "You have brought the day you announced".

v: How[^1] the Lord in his anger has covered Daughter Zion[^2] with a cloud![^3] He has thrown down from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel; he has not remembered his footstool[^4] in the day of his anger.
אֵיכָה֩ יָעִ֨יב בְּאַפּ֤וֹ ׀ אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן הִשְׁלִ֤יךְ מִשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔רֶץ תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹא־זָכַ֥ר הֲדֹם־רַגְלָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ׃ ס

The Lord has swallowed up without pity all the dwellings of Jacob. In his fury he has torn down the strongholds of Daughter Judah; he has brought them down to the ground. He has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
בִּלַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֜י *לא **וְלֹ֣א חָמַ֗ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־נְא֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֔ב הָרַ֧ס בְּעֶבְרָת֛וֹ מִבְצְרֵ֥י בַת־יְהוּדָ֖ה הִגִּ֣יעַ לָאָ֑רֶץ חִלֵּ֥ל מַמְלָכָ֖ה וְשָׂרֶֽיהָ׃ ס
In his burning anger he has cut off every horn[^5] of Israel. He has drawn back his right hand in the face of the enemy. He has burned against Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes all around.
גָּדַ֣ע בָּֽחֳרִי אַ֗ף כֹּ֚ל קֶ֣רֶן יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵשִׁ֥יב אָח֛וֹר יְמִינ֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב וַיִּבְעַ֤ר בְּיַעֲקֹב֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ לֶֽהָבָ֔ה אָכְלָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃ ס
He has bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand is set like a foe's. He has killed all who were pleasing to the eye. On the tent of Daughter Zion he has poured out his wrath like fire.
דָּרַ֨ךְ קַשְׁתּ֜וֹ כְּאוֹיֵ֗ב נִצָּ֤ב יְמִינוֹ֙ כְּצָ֔ר וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֔ג כֹּ֖ל מַחֲמַדֵּי־עָ֑יִן בְּאֹ֙הֶל֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן שָׁפַ֥ךְ כָּאֵ֖שׁ חֲמָתֽוֹ׃ ס
The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces; he has destroyed his strongholds.[^6] He has multiplied mourning and moaning[^7] in Daughter Judah.
הָיָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ כְּאוֹיֵב֙ בִּלַּ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּלַּע֙ כָּל־אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שִׁחֵ֖ת מִבְצָרָ֑יו וַיֶּ֙רֶב֙ בְּבַת־יְהוּדָ֔ה תַּאֲנִיָּ֖ה וַאֲנִיָּֽה׃ ס
He has wrecked his booth[^8] like a garden; he has destroyed his place of meeting.[^9] The LORD[^10] has made Zion forget festival and Sabbath, and in his fierce anger he has spurned king and priest.
וַיַּחְמֹ֤ס כַּגַּן֙ שֻׂכּ֔וֹ שִׁחֵ֖ת מוֹעֲד֑וֹ שִׁכַּ֨ח יְהוָ֤ה ׀ בְּצִיּוֹן֙ מוֹעֵ֣ד וְשַׁבָּ֔ת וַיִּנְאַ֥ץ בְּזַֽעַם־אַפּ֖וֹ מֶ֥לֶךְ וְכֹהֵֽן׃ ס
The Lord has rejected his altar and disowned his sanctuary. He has handed over to the enemy the walls of her palaces. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a festival day.
זָנַ֨ח אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ מִזְבְּחוֹ֙ נִאֵ֣ר מִקְדָּשׁ֔וֹ הִסְגִּיר֙ בְּיַד־אוֹיֵ֔ב חוֹמֹ֖ת אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ ק֛וֹל נָתְנ֥וּ בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֖ה כְּי֥וֹם מוֹעֵֽד׃ ס

The LORD determined to destroy the wall of Daughter Zion. He stretched out the measuring line; he did not hold back his hand from destroying.[^11] He made rampart and wall lament; together they languish.
חָשַׁ֨ב יְהוָ֤ה ׀ לְהַשְׁחִית֙ חוֹמַ֣ת בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן נָ֣טָה קָ֔ו לֹא־הֵשִׁ֥יב יָד֖וֹ מִבַּלֵּ֑עַ וַיּֽ͏ַאֲבֶל־חֵ֥ל וְחוֹמָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֥ו אֻמְלָֽלוּ׃ ס
Her gates have sunk into the ground; he has ruined and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no instruction,[^12] and her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
טָבְע֤וּ בָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁעָרֶ֔יהָ אִבַּ֥ד וְשִׁבַּ֖ר בְּרִיחֶ֑יהָ מַלְכָּ֨הּ וְשָׂרֶ֤יהָ בַגּוֹיִם֙ אֵ֣ין תּוֹרָ֔ה גַּם־נְבִיאֶ֕יהָ לֹא־מָצְא֥וּ חָז֖וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃ ס
The elders of Daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
יֵשְׁב֨וּ לָאָ֤רֶץ יִדְּמוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בַת־צִיּ֔וֹן הֶֽעֱל֤וּ עָפָר֙ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔ם חָגְר֖וּ שַׂקִּ֑ים הוֹרִ֤ידוּ לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ רֹאשָׁ֔ן בְּתוּלֹ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס

My eyes are worn out with tears; my insides churn. My heart is poured out on the ground[^13] because of the destruction of my dear people,[^14] because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
כָּל֨וּ בַדְּמָע֤וֹת עֵינַי֙ חֳמַרְמְר֣וּ מֵעַ֔י נִשְׁפַּ֤ךְ לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ כְּבֵדִ֔י עַל־שֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־עַמִּ֑י בֵּֽעָטֵ֤ף עוֹלֵל֙ וְיוֹנֵ֔ק בִּרְחֹב֖וֹת קִרְיָֽה׃ ס
They say to their mothers, "Where is the grain and the wine?" as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their life is poured out on their mothers' laps.
לְאִמֹּתָם֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ אַיֵּ֖ה דָּגָ֣ן וָיָ֑יִן בְּהִֽתְעַטְּפָ֤ם כֶּֽחָלָל֙ בִּרְחֹב֣וֹת עִ֔יר בְּהִשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשָׁ֔ם אֶל־חֵ֖יק אִמֹּתָֽם׃ ס
What can I say for you?[^15] To what can I compare you, Daughter Jerusalem? What can I liken to you, to comfort you, Virgin Daughter Zion? For your ruin is as vast as the sea; who can heal you?
מָֽה־אֲעִידֵ֞ךְ מָ֣ה אֲדַמֶּה־לָּ֗ךְ הַבַּת֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מָ֤ה אַשְׁוֶה־לָּךְ֙ וַאֲנַֽחֲמֵ֔ךְ בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־צִיּ֑וֹן כִּֽי־גָד֥וֹל כַּיָּ֛ם שִׁבְרֵ֖ךְ מִ֥י יִרְפָּא־לָֽךְ׃ ס
Your prophets have seen for you visions that were empty and false;[^16] they did not expose your guilt to restore your fortunes. They have seen for you oracles that were empty and misleading.
נְבִיאַ֗יִךְ חָ֤זוּ לָךְ֙ שָׁ֣וְא וְתָפֵ֔ל וְלֹֽא־גִלּ֥וּ עַל־עֲוֺנֵ֖ךְ לְהָשִׁ֣יב *שביתך **שְׁבוּתֵ֑ךְ וַיֶּ֣חֱזוּ לָ֔ךְ מַשְׂא֥וֹת שָׁ֖וְא וּמַדּוּחִֽים׃ ס
All who pass along the road clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?"[^17]
סָֽפְק֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ כַּפַּ֙יִם֙ כָּל־עֹ֣בְרֵי דֶ֔רֶךְ שָֽׁרְקוּ֙ וַיָּנִ֣עוּ רֹאשָׁ֔ם עַל־בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם הֲזֹ֣את הָעִ֗יר שֶׁיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כְּלִ֣ילַת יֹ֔פִי מָשׂ֖וֹשׂ לְכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ ס
All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and grind their teeth. They say, "We have swallowed her up! Ah, this is the day we hoped for; we have found it, we have seen it!"
פָּצ֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ פִּיהֶם֙ כָּל־א֣וֹיְבַ֔יִךְ שָֽׁרְקוּ֙ וַיַּֽחַרְקוּ־שֵׁ֔ן אָמְר֖וּ בִּלָּ֑עְנוּ אַ֣ךְ זֶ֥ה הַיּ֛וֹם שֶׁקִּוִּינֻ֖הוּ מָצָ֥אנוּ רָאִֽינוּ׃ ס

The LORD has done what he planned; he has carried out his word, which he commanded in days of old. He has torn down without pity; he has let the enemy rejoice over you; he has raised up the horn of your foes.
עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָמָ֗ם בִּצַּ֤ע אֶמְרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֔דֶם הָרַ֖ס וְלֹ֣א חָמָ֑ל וַיְשַׂמַּ֤ח עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ אוֹיֵ֔ב הֵרִ֖ים קֶ֥רֶן צָרָֽיִךְ׃ ס
Their heart cried out to the Lord. O wall of Daughter Zion,[^18] let your tears run down like a torrent day and night! Give yourself no relief; do not let your eyes rest.[^19]
צָעַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם אֶל־אֲדֹנָ֑י חוֹמַ֣ת בַּת־צִ֠יּוֹן הוֹרִ֨ידִי כַנַּ֤חַל דִּמְעָה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אַֽל־תִּתְּנִ֤י פוּגַת֙ לָ֔ךְ אַל־תִּדֹּ֖ם בַּת־עֵינֵֽךְ׃ ס

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the night watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your children, who faint with hunger at the head of every street.

ק֣וּמִי ׀ רֹ֣נִּי *בליל **בַלַּ֗יְלָה לְרֹאשׁ֙ אַשְׁמֻר֔וֹת שִׁפְכִ֤י כַמַּ֙יִם֙ לִבֵּ֔ךְ נֹ֖כַח פְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י שְׂאִ֧י אֵלָ֣יו כַּפַּ֗יִךְ עַל־נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ עֽוֹלָלַ֔יִךְ הָעֲטוּפִ֥ים בְּרָעָ֖ב בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־חוּצֽוֹת׃ ס
Look, LORD, and consider: to whom have you done this?[^20] Should women eat their offspring, the children they have cared for?[^21] Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה לְמִ֖י עוֹלַ֣לְתָּ כֹּ֑ה אִם־תֹּאכַ֨לְנָה נָשִׁ֤ים פִּרְיָם֙ עֹלֲלֵ֣י טִפֻּחִ֔ים אִם־יֵהָרֵ֛ג בְּמִקְדַּ֥שׁ אֲדֹנָ֖י כֹּהֵ֥ן וְנָבִֽיא׃ ס
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed them on the day of your anger; you have slaughtered without pity.
שָׁכְב֨וּ לָאָ֤רֶץ חוּצוֹת֙ נַ֣עַר וְזָקֵ֔ן בְּתוּלֹתַ֥י וּבַחוּרַ֖י נָפְל֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב הָרַגְ֙תָּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אַפֶּ֔ךָ טָבַ֖חְתָּ לֹ֥א חָמָֽלְתָּ׃ ס
You summoned, as for a festival day, my terrors from all around.[^22] On the day of the LORD's anger, no one escaped or survived. Those I cared for and raised, my enemy has destroyed.
תִּקְרָא֩ כְי֨וֹם מוֹעֵ֤ד מְגוּרַי֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם אַף־יְהוָ֖ה פָּלִ֣יט וְשָׂרִ֑יד אֲשֶׁר־טִפַּ֥חְתִּי וְרִבִּ֖יתִי אֹיְבִ֥י כִלָּֽם׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *eikhah*, "How!"; see 1:1. Like chapter 1, this chapter is an acrostic poem: its twenty-two verses begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order. Here the letter *pe* (verse 16) comes before *ayin* (verse 17), as in chapters 3 and 4. Each verse has three lines, except verse 19, which has four.
n.3: Hebrew *ya'iv*, a word found only here, probably "has covered with a cloud". Or "has treated with contempt".
n.4: That is, the temple, or the ark of the covenant in it (Psalm 99:5; 132:7; 1 Chronicles 28:2).
n.5: A picture of strength. Also in verse 17.
n.6: The Hebrew changes from "her" to "his", both referring to Israel.
n.8: That is, the temple. Hebrew *sukko*, "his booth" or "his shelter".
n.9: Or "his appointed festival". Hebrew *mo'ed*, the word translated "festival" later in the verse.
n.10: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.12: Or "the law is no more". Hebrew *torah*, the teaching given by the priests.
n.13: Literally "My liver". The poet speaks in verses 11–19.
n.14: Literally "the daughter of my people", a tender way of speaking of the people as a young woman. Also in 3:48; 4:3, 6, 10.
n.15: Or "What witness can I bring for you?" The meaning of the verb is uncertain.
n.17: Compare Psalm 48:3 (48:2 in English Bibles) and 50:2.
n.18: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "Their heart cried out to the Lord, wall of Daughter Zion".
n.19: Literally "do not let the daughter of your eye be still". The "daughter of the eye" is the pupil.
n.21: Hebrew *tippuchim*, a word found only here, "tender care". Compare "cared for" in verse 22.
n.22: Compare "terror on every side" in Jeremiah 6:25; 20:10.

v: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath.[^1]
אֲנִ֤י הַגֶּ֙בֶר֙ רָאָ֣ה עֳנִ֔י בְּשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָתֽוֹ׃
He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness, not light.
אוֹתִ֥י נָהַ֛ג וַיֹּלַ֖ךְ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־אֽוֹר׃
Surely against me he turns his hand again and again, all day long.
אַ֣ךְ בִּ֥י יָשֻׁ֛ב יַהֲפֹ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃ ס
He has worn away my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones.
בִּלָּ֤ה בְשָׂרִי֙ וְעוֹרִ֔י שִׁבַּ֖ר עַצְמוֹתָֽי׃
He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness[^2] and hardship.
בָּנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י וַיַּקַּ֖ף רֹ֥אשׁ וּתְלָאָֽה׃
He has made me live in dark places, like those long dead.[^3]
בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּ֥ים הוֹשִׁיבַ֖נִי כְּמֵתֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃ ס
He has walled me in so that I cannot get out; he has made my chains heavy.[^4]
גָּדַ֧ר בַּעֲדִ֛י וְלֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א הִכְבִּ֥יד נְחָשְׁתִּֽי׃
Though I call out and cry for help, he shuts out my prayer.
גַּ֣ם כִּ֤י אֶזְעַק֙ וַאֲשַׁוֵּ֔עַ שָׂתַ֖ם תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃
He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; he has made my paths crooked.
גָּדַ֤ר דְּרָכַי֙ בְּגָזִ֔ית נְתִיבֹתַ֖י עִוָּֽה׃ ס
He is to me a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding.
דֹּ֣ב אֹרֵ֥ב הוּא֙ לִ֔י *אריה **אֲרִ֖י בְּמִסְתָּרִֽים׃
He has turned aside my ways and torn me to pieces; he has made me desolate.
דְּרָכַ֥י סוֹרֵ֛ר וַֽיְפַשְּׁחֵ֖נִי שָׂמַ֥נִי שֹׁמֵֽם׃
He bent his bow and set me up as a target for his arrow.
דָּרַ֤ךְ קַשְׁתוֹ֙ וַיַּצִּיבֵ֔נִי כַּמַּטָּרָ֖א לַחֵֽץ׃ ס
He has shot into my heart[^5] the arrows of his quiver.[^6]
הֵבִיא֙ בְּכִלְיוֹתָ֔י בְּנֵ֖י אַשְׁפָּתֽוֹ׃
I have become a laughingstock to all my people,[^7] their mocking song all day long.
הָיִ֤יתִי שְּׂחֹק֙ לְכָל־עַמִּ֔י נְגִינָתָ֖ם כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
He has filled me with bitter herbs; he has made me drink my fill of wormwood.
הִשְׂבִּיעַ֥נִי בַמְּרוֹרִ֖ים הִרְוַ֥נִי לַעֲנָֽה׃ ס
He has broken my teeth with gravel; he has pressed me down in the ashes.
וַיַּגְרֵ֤ס בֶּֽחָצָץ֙ שִׁנָּ֔י הִכְפִּישַׁ֖נִי בָּאֵֽפֶר׃
My soul has been rejected from peace;[^8] I have forgotten what good is.
וַתִּזְנַ֧ח מִשָּׁל֛וֹם נַפְשִׁ֖י נָשִׁ֥יתִי טוֹבָֽה׃
So I said, "My strength has perished, and my hope from the LORD."[^9]
וָאֹמַר֙ אָבַ֣ד נִצְחִ֔י וְתוֹחַלְתִּ֖י מֵיְהוָֽה׃ ס
Remember my affliction and my homelessness, the wormwood and the bitterness.[^10]
זְכָר־עָנְיִ֥י וּמְרוּדִ֖י לַעֲנָ֥ה וָרֹֽאשׁ׃
My soul remembers it continually and is bowed down within me.[^11]
זָכ֣וֹר תִּזְכּ֔וֹר *ותשיח **וְתָשׁ֥וֹחַ עָלַ֖י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
But this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
זֹ֛את אָשִׁ֥יב אֶל־לִבִּ֖י עַל־כֵּ֥ן אוֹחִֽיל׃ ס
Because of the LORD's faithful love[^12] we are not finished,[^13] for his compassion does not fail.
חַֽסְדֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י לֹא־תָ֔מְנוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כָל֖וּ רַחֲמָֽיו׃
It is new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
חֲדָשִׁים֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים רַבָּ֖ה אֱמוּנָתֶֽךָ׃
"The LORD is my portion," says my soul, "therefore I will hope in him."
חֶלְקִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אָמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י עַל־כֵּ֖ן אוֹחִ֥יל לֽוֹ׃ ס
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
ט֤וֹב יְהוָה֙ לְקֹוָ֔ו לְנֶ֖פֶשׁ תִּדְרְשֶֽׁנּוּ׃
It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the LORD.
ט֤וֹב וְיָחִיל֙ וְדוּמָ֔ם לִתְשׁוּעַ֖ת יְהוָֽה׃
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
ט֣וֹב לַגֶּ֔בֶר כִּֽי־יִשָּׂ֥א עֹ֖ל בִּנְעוּרָֽיו׃ ס
Let him sit alone in silence, for he has laid it on him.[^14]
יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּדָד֙ וְיִדֹּ֔ם כִּ֥י נָטַ֖ל עָלָֽיו׃
Let him put his mouth in the dust; perhaps there may yet be hope.
יִתֵּ֤ן בֶּֽעָפָר֙ פִּ֔יהוּ אוּלַ֖י יֵ֥שׁ תִּקְוָֽה׃
Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with disgrace.
יִתֵּ֧ן לְמַכֵּ֛הוּ לֶ֖חִי יִשְׂבַּ֥ע בְּחֶרְפָּֽה׃ ס
For the Lord will not reject forever.
כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יִזְנַ֛ח לְעוֹלָ֖ם אֲדֹנָֽי׃
Though he brings grief, he will have compassion according to the greatness of his faithful love.
כִּ֣י אִם־הוֹגָ֔ה וְרִחַ֖ם כְּרֹ֥ב *חסדו **חֲסָדָֽיו׃
For he does not afflict willingly,[^15] or bring grief to human beings.
כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עִנָּה֙ מִלִבּ֔וֹ וַיַּגֶּ֖ה בְ[t]נֵי־אִֽישׁ׃ ס
To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the land,
לְדַכֵּא֙ תַּ֣חַת רַגְלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל אֲסִ֥ירֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
to deny a man his rights before the Most High,[^16]
לְהַטּוֹת֙ מִשְׁפַּט־גָּ֔בֶר נֶ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֥י עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
to wrong a person in his lawsuit: the Lord does not approve.[^17]
לְעַוֵּ֤ת אָדָם֙ בְּרִיב֔וֹ אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃ ס
Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?
מִ֣י זֶ֤ה אָמַר֙ וַתֶּ֔הִי אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א צִוָּֽה׃
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both evil and good come?
מִפִּ֤י עֶלְיוֹן֙ לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֔א הָרָע֖וֹת וְהַטּֽוֹב׃
Why should any living person complain, any man, about his sins?[^18]
מַה־יִּתְאוֹנֵן֙ אָדָ֣ם חָ֔י גֶּ֖בֶר עַל־*חטאו **חֲטָאָֽיו׃ ס
Let us search and examine our ways, and return to the LORD.
נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה דְרָכֵ֙ינוּ֙ וְֽנַחְקֹ֔רָה וְנָשׁ֖וּבָה עַד־יְהוָֽה׃
Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in heaven:
נִשָּׂ֤א לְבָבֵ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־כַּפָּ֔יִם אֶל־אֵ֖ל בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
We have rebelled and disobeyed, and you have not forgiven.
נַ֤חְנוּ פָשַׁ֙עְנוּ֙ וּמָרִ֔ינוּ אַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א סָלָֽחְתָּ׃ ס
You have wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you have killed without pity.
סַכֹּ֤תָה בָאַף֙ וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ הָרַ֖גְתָּ לֹ֥א חָמָֽלְתָּ׃
You have wrapped yourself in a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
סַכּ֤וֹתָה בֶֽעָנָן֙ לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲב֖וֹר תְּפִלָּֽה׃
You have made us scum and refuse among the peoples.
סְחִ֧י וּמָא֛וֹס תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעַמִּֽים׃ ס
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
פָּצ֥וּ עָלֵ֛ינוּ פִּיהֶ֖ם כָּל־אֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃
Panic and pit have come upon us,[^19] devastation and destruction.
פַּ֧חַד וָפַ֛חַת הָ֥יָה לָ֖נוּ הַשֵּׁ֥את וְהַשָּֽׁבֶר׃
My eye runs down with streams of water because of the destruction of my dear people.[^20]
פַּלְגֵי־מַ֙יִם֙ תֵּרַ֣ד עֵינִ֔י עַל־שֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃ ס
My eye flows and does not stop, without any rest,
עֵינִ֧י נִגְּרָ֛ה וְלֹ֥א תִדְמֶ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין הֲפֻגֽוֹת׃
until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
עַד־יַשְׁקִ֣יף וְיֵ֔רֶא יְהוָ֖ה מִשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
My eye brings grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
עֵינִי֙ עֽוֹלְלָ֣ה לְנַפְשִׁ֔י מִכֹּ֖ל בְּנ֥וֹת עִירִֽי׃ ס
Those who are my enemies without cause have hunted me down like a bird.
צ֥וֹד צָד֛וּנִי כַּצִּפּ֖וֹר אֹיְבַ֥י חִנָּֽם׃
They tried to end my life in a pit,[^21] and they threw stones at me.[^22]
צָֽמְת֤וּ בַבּוֹר֙ חַיָּ֔י וַיַּדּוּ־אֶ֖בֶן בִּֽי׃
Water flowed over my head; I said, "I am cut off!"
צָֽפוּ־מַ֥יִם עַל־רֹאשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥רְתִּי נִגְזָֽרְתִּי׃ ס
I called on your name, LORD, from the depths of the pit.
קָרָ֤אתִי שִׁמְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה מִבּ֖וֹר תַּחְתִּיּֽוֹת׃
You heard my voice; do not close your ear to my cry for relief, to my cry for help!
קוֹלִ֖י שָׁמָ֑עְתָּ אַל־תַּעְלֵ֧ם אָזְנְךָ֛ לְרַוְחָתִ֖י לְשַׁוְעָתִֽי׃
You came near on the day I called to you; you said, "Do not fear!"
קָרַ֙בְתָּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֶקְרָאֶ֔ךָּ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אַל־תִּירָֽא׃ ס
You have taken up my case, Lord; you have redeemed my life.
רַ֧בְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֛י רִיבֵ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י גָּאַ֥לְתָּ חַיָּֽי׃
You have seen the wrong done to me, LORD; judge my case!
רָאִ֤יתָה יְהוָה֙ עַוָּ֣תָתִ֔י שָׁפְטָ֖ה מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
רָאִ֙יתָה֙ כָּל־נִקְמָתָ֔ם כָּל־מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃ ס
You have heard their taunts, LORD, all their plots against me,
שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתָם֙ יְהוָ֔ה כָּל־מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖ם עָלָֽי׃
the lips of those who rise against me, and their muttering against me all day long.
שִׂפְתֵ֤י קָמַי֙ וְהֶגְיוֹנָ֔ם עָלַ֖י כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
Look at them, sitting or standing:[^23] I am their mocking song.
שִׁבְתָּ֤ם וְקִֽימָתָם֙ הַבִּ֔יטָה אֲנִ֖י מַנְגִּינָתָֽם׃ ס
Pay them back, LORD,[^24] according to the work of their hands.
תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
Give them a hardened heart;[^25] may your curse be on them!
תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת־לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם׃
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.[^26]
תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ פ

n.1: This chapter is a triple acrostic. It has sixty-six verses, and each letter of the Hebrew alphabet begins three verses in a row: verses 1–3 begin with *alef*, verses 4–6 with *bet*, and so on to *tav* in verses 64–66. As in chapters 2 and 4, *pe* (verses 46–48) comes before *ayin* (verses 49–51). The speaker is one man, who speaks of God as "he" until verse 18.
n.2: Hebrew *rosh*, a bitter, poisonous plant. Also in verse 19.
n.3: The same words are in Psalm 143:3.
n.4: Literally "my bronze", that is, my bronze chains.
n.7: Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac read "all peoples".
n.8: Or "You have rejected my soul from peace".
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Or "The memory of my affliction and my homelessness is wormwood and bitterness".
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "and my soul muses (or complains)" but read "and my soul is bowed down". Or "You will surely remember, and my soul is bowed down within me".
n.12: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Here and in verse 32 the word is plural, "acts of faithful love".
n.13: Literally "The faithful love of the LORD, for we are not finished". The Syriac and the Targum read "it is not finished", matching the next line; this reading is followed by many translations.
n.14: Or "when it has been laid on him".
n.16: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God. Also in verse 38.
n.17: Literally "the Lord does not see". Or "does the Lord not see?"
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "his sin" but read "his sins". Or "Why should a living person complain? Let each one complain about his own sins".
n.19: A play on sounds: *pachad va-fachat*. Compare Isaiah 24:17; Jeremiah 48:43.
n.20: Literally "the daughter of my people"; see 2:11.
n.21: Hebrew *bor*, a pit or cistern, also a picture of the grave. Also in verse 55.
n.22: Or "they set a stone over me".
n.24: Or "You will pay them back, LORD"; also in verses 65–66.
n.25: Hebrew *meginnat lev*, a phrase found only here, perhaps "a covering of the heart", that is, a hardened or anguished heart.
n.26: The Septuagint reads "under heaven, O Lord".

v: How[^1] the gold has grown dim, how the pure gold has changed! The holy stones[^2] lie scattered at the head of every street.
אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב יִשְׁנֶ֖א הַכֶּ֣תֶם הַטּ֑וֹב תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֙כְנָה֙ אַבְנֵי־קֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּרֹ֖אשׁ כָּל־חוּצֽוֹת׃ ס
The precious children of Zion, worth their weight in fine gold, how they are regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands!
בְּנֵ֤י צִיּוֹן֙ הַיְקָרִ֔ים הַמְסֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑ז אֵיכָ֤ה נֶחְשְׁבוּ֙ לְנִבְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶשׂ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י יוֹצֵֽר׃ ס
Even jackals[^3] offer the breast and nurse their young, but my dear people[^4] has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.[^5]
גַּם־*תנין **תַּנִּים֙ חָ֣לְצוּ שַׁ֔ד הֵינִ֖יקוּ גּוּרֵיהֶ֑ן בַּת־עַמִּ֣י לְאַכְזָ֔ר *כי *ענים **כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃ ס
The tongue of the nursing infant sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst. Little children ask for bread, but no one breaks it for them.
דָּבַ֨ק לְשׁ֥וֹן יוֹנֵ֛ק אֶל־חִ[t]כּ֖וֹ בַּצָּמָ֑א עֽוֹלָלִים֙ שָׁ֣אֲלוּ לֶ֔חֶם פֹּרֵ֖שׂ אֵ֥ין לָהֶֽם׃ ס
Those who used to eat delicacies are desolate in the streets. Those brought up in scarlet now cling to ash heaps.
הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ לְמַ֣עֲדַנִּ֔ים נָשַׁ֖מּוּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת הָאֱמֻנִים֙ עֲלֵ֣י תוֹלָ֔ע חִבְּק֖וּ אַשְׁפַּתּֽוֹת׃ ס
The punishment[^6] of my dear people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, with no hand laid on it.[^7]
וַיִּגְדַּל֙ עֲוֺ֣ן בַּת־עַמִּ֔י מֵֽחַטַּ֖את סְדֹ֑ם הַֽהֲפוּכָ֣ה כְמוֹ־רָ֔גַע וְלֹא־חָ֥לוּ בָ֖הּ יָדָֽיִם׃ ס
Her princes[^8] were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were ruddier than coral,[^9] their form like sapphire.[^10]
זַכּ֤וּ נְזִירֶ֙יהָ֙ מִשֶּׁ֔[t]לֶג צַח֖וּ מֵחָלָ֑ב אָ֤דְמוּ עֶ֙צֶם֙ מִפְּנִינִ֔ים סַפִּ֖יר גִּזְרָתָֽם׃ ס
Now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as wood.
חָשַׁ֤ךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר֙ תָּֽאֳרָ֔ם לֹ֥א נִכְּר֖וּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת צָפַ֤ד עוֹרָם֙ עַל־עַצְמָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה כָעֵֽץ׃ ס
Better off were those killed by the sword than those killed by hunger, who waste away, pierced through by the lack of the produce of the field.[^11]
טוֹבִ֤ים הָיוּ֙ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵֽחַלְלֵ֖י רָעָ֑ב שֶׁ֣הֵ֤ם יָז֙וּבוּ֙ מְדֻקָּרִ֔ים מִתְּנוּבֹ֖ת שָׂדָֽי׃ ס
The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food in the destruction of my dear people.
יְדֵ֗י נָשִׁים֙ רַחֲמָ֣נִיּ֔וֹת בִּשְּׁל֖וּ יַלְדֵיהֶ֑ן הָי֤וּ לְבָרוֹת֙ לָ֔מוֹ בְּשֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃ ס
The LORD[^12] has spent his wrath; he has poured out his burning anger. He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.
כִּלָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־חֲמָת֔וֹ שָׁפַ֖ךְ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּצֶּת־אֵ֣שׁ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וַתֹּ֖אכַל יְסוֹדֹתֶֽיהָ׃ ס
The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did any of the inhabitants of the world, that foe and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
לֹ֤א הֶאֱמִ֙ינוּ֙ מַלְכֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ *וכל **כֹּ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל כִּ֤י יָבֹא֙ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס
It happened because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests,[^13] who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
מֵֽחַטֹּ֣את נְבִיאֶ֔יהָ עֲוֺנ֖וֹת כֹּהֲנֶ֑יהָ הַשֹּׁפְכִ֥ים בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ דַּ֥ם צַדִּיקִֽים׃ ס
They wandered blind through the streets, so defiled with blood that no one could touch their garments.
נָע֤וּ עִוְרִים֙ בַּֽחוּצ֔וֹת נְגֹֽאֲל֖וּ בַּדָּ֑ם בְּלֹ֣א יֽוּכְל֔וּ יִגְּע֖וּ בִּלְבֻשֵׁיהֶֽם׃ ס
"Go away! Unclean!" people cried to them. "Go away, go away! Do not touch!" So they fled and wandered, and people among the nations said, "They shall not stay here any longer."[^14]
ס֣וּרוּ טָמֵ֞א קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֗מוֹ ס֤וּרוּ ס֙וּרוּ֙ אַל־תִּגָּ֔עוּ כִּ֥י נָצ֖וּ גַּם־נָ֑עוּ אָֽמְרוּ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יפוּ לָגֽוּר׃ ס
The LORD himself[^15] has scattered them; he will no longer look on them. No one showed respect to the priests, or favor to the elders.
פְּנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ חִלְּקָ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַבִּיטָ֑ם פְּנֵ֤י כֹהֲנִים֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔אוּ *זקנים **ו[q]**זְקֵנִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָנָֽנוּ׃ ס
Our eyes still wear themselves out, looking in vain[^16] for help. From our watchtower we watched for a nation that could not save us.
*עודינה **עוֹדֵ֙ינוּ֙ תִּכְלֶ֣ינָה עֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֶל־עֶזְרָתֵ֖נוּ הָ֑בֶל בְּצִפִּיָּתֵ֣נוּ צִפִּ֔ינוּ אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃ ס
They dogged our steps so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near; our days were numbered,[^17] for our end had come.
צָד֣וּ צְעָדֵ֔ינוּ מִלֶּ֖כֶת בִּרְחֹבֹתֵ֑ינוּ קָרַ֥ב קִצֵּ֛ינוּ מָלְא֥וּ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כִּי־בָ֥א קִצֵּֽינוּ׃ ס
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles[^18] in the sky. They chased us on the mountains; they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
קַלִּ֤ים הָיוּ֙ רֹדְפֵ֔ינוּ מִנִּשְׁרֵ֖י שָׁמָ֑יִם עַל־הֶהָרִ֣ים דְּלָקֻ֔נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר אָ֥רְבוּ לָֽנוּ׃ ס
The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed,[^19] was caught in their pits, the one of whom we said, "Under his shadow we will live among the nations."
ר֤וּחַ אַפֵּ֙ינוּ֙ מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה נִלְכַּ֖ד בִּשְׁחִיתוֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְנוּ בְּצִלּ֖וֹ נִֽחְיֶ֥ה בַגּוֹיִֽם׃ ס
Rejoice and be glad, Daughter Edom,[^20] you who live in the land of Uz![^21] To you also the cup will pass;[^22] you will become drunk and strip yourself naked.
שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם *יושבתי **יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ע֑וּץ גַּם־עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ תַּעֲבָר־כּ֔וֹס תִּשְׁכְּרִ֖י וְתִתְעָרִֽי׃ ס
Your punishment is complete, Daughter Zion; he will not keep you in exile any longer. But he will punish your iniquity, Daughter Edom; he will expose your sins.
תַּם־עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַגְלוֹתֵ֑ךְ פָּקַ֤ד עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם גִּלָּ֖ה עַל־חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *eikhah*, "How!"; see 1:1. This chapter is an acrostic poem: its twenty-two verses begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, with *pe* (verse 16) before *ayin* (verse 17), as in chapters 2 and 3. Each verse here has two lines.
n.2: Perhaps the stones of the temple, or precious stones, a picture of the "precious children" of verse 2.
n.3: The Hebrew text is written *tannin*, which can mean "sea monster" or be another plural form of "jackals", but read *tannim*, "jackals".
n.4: Literally "the daughter of my people"; see 2:11. Also in verses 6 and 10.
n.5: The ostrich was thought to neglect its young (Job 39:13–16).
n.6: Or "iniquity". Hebrew *avon* means both the wrong and its punishment, and *chatta't*, "sin", later in the verse, can also mean its punishment. Also in verse 22.
n.7: Literally "and no hands whirled against it". Or "and no hands were wrung over it".
n.9: Hebrew *peninim*, perhaps red coral, or pearls.
n.10: Hebrew *sappir*, probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone.
n.11: Literally "who flow away, pierced, from the produce of the field".
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Literally "From the sins of her prophets, the iniquities of her priests".
n.14: Or "They shall not live among us as foreigners any longer".
n.16: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the key word of Ecclesiastes; here "in vain".
n.19: That is, the king of Judah, probably Zedekiah, who was captured as he fled (2 Kings 25:4–7).
n.20: A poetic name for Edom and its people, like "Daughter Zion" for Jerusalem (1:6). Also in verse 22.
n.21: A land to the east or southeast of Israel; compare Job 1:1.
n.22: The cup of God's wrath, which the nations must drink (Jeremiah 25:15–29).

v: Remember, LORD,[^1] what has happened to us; look and see our disgrace.[^2]
זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה־הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ *הביט **הַבִּ֖יטָה וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת־חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
נַחֲלָתֵ֙נוּ֙ נֶֽהֶפְכָ֣ה לְזָרִ֔ים בָּתֵּ֖ינוּ לְנָכְרִֽים׃
We have become orphans, without a father; our mothers are like widows.
יְתוֹמִ֤ים הָיִ֙ינוּ֙ *אין **וְאֵ֣ין אָ֔ב אִמֹּתֵ֖ינוּ כְּאַלְמָנֽוֹת׃
We must pay silver for the water we drink; our wood comes to us at a price.
מֵימֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּכֶ֣סֶף שָׁתִ֔ינוּ עֵצֵ֖ינוּ בִּמְחִ֥יר יָבֹֽאוּ׃
Our pursuers are at our necks;[^3] we are weary and are given no rest.
עַ֤ל צַוָּארֵ֙נוּ֙ נִרְדָּ֔פְנוּ יָגַ֖עְנוּ *לא **וְלֹ֥א הֽוּנַ֖ח לָֽנוּ׃
We have given our hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to get enough bread.[^4]
מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ נָתַ֣נּוּ יָ֔ד אַשּׁ֖וּר לִשְׂבֹּ֥עַֽ לָֽחֶם׃
Our ancestors sinned and are no more, and we bear their iniquities.
אֲבֹתֵ֤ינוּ חָֽטְאוּ֙ *אינם **וְאֵינָ֔ם *אנחנו **וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ עֲוֺנֹתֵיהֶ֥ם סָבָֽלְנוּ׃
Slaves[^5] rule over us; there is no one to rescue us from their hand.
עֲבָדִים֙ מָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֔נוּ פֹּרֵ֖ק אֵ֥ין מִיָּדָֽם׃
We get our bread at the risk of our lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.
בְּנַפְשֵׁ֙נוּ֙ נָבִ֣יא לַחְמֵ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
Our skin is hot as an oven from the burning heat of hunger.
עוֹרֵ֙נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב׃
Women have been raped in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
Princes have been hung up by their hands;[^6] elders are shown no respect.
שָׂרִים֙ בְּיָדָ֣ם נִתְל֔וּ פְּנֵ֥י זְקֵנִ֖ים לֹ֥א נֶהְדָּֽרוּ׃
Young men carry the millstone,[^7] and boys stagger under loads of wood.
בַּחוּרִים֙ טְח֣וֹן נָשָׂ֔אוּ וּנְעָרִ֖ים בָּעֵ֥ץ כָּשָֽׁלוּ׃
The elders have left the city gate; the young men have stopped their music.
זְקֵנִים֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר שָׁבָ֔תוּ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מִנְּגִינָתָֽם׃
The joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ לִבֵּ֔נוּ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְאֵ֖בֶל מְחֹלֵֽנוּ׃
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ אֽוֹי־נָ֥א לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ׃
Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes have grown dim:
עַל־זֶ֗ה הָיָ֤ה דָוֶה֙ לִבֵּ֔נוּ עַל־אֵ֖לֶּה חָשְׁכ֥וּ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃
because Mount Zion lies desolate, with foxes prowling over it.
עַ֤ל הַר־צִיּוֹן֙ שֶׁשָּׁמֵ֔ם שׁוּעָלִ֖ים הִלְּכוּ־בֽוֹ׃ פ
But you, LORD, reign forever;[^8] your throne endures from generation to generation.
אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֔ב כִּסְאֲךָ֖ לְדֹ֥ר וָדֽוֹר׃
Why do you forget us forever? Why do you forsake us for so long?
לָ֤מָּה לָנֶ֙צַח֙ תִּשְׁכָּחֵ֔נוּ תַּֽעַזְבֵ֖נוּ לְאֹ֥רֶךְ יָמִֽים׃
Bring us back to you, LORD, so that we may return; renew our days as of old,
הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ *ונשוב **וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה חַדֵּ֥שׁ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כְּקֶֽדֶם׃
unless you have utterly rejected us, and are angry with us beyond measure.[^9]
כִּ֚י אִם־מָאֹ֣ס מְאַסְתָּ֔נוּ קָצַ֥פְתָּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ עַד־מְאֹֽד׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: This chapter has twenty-two verses, as many as the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, but unlike chapters 1–4 it is not an acrostic. Its lines are shorter, and the whole chapter is a prayer of the people ("we").
n.3: Literally "On our necks we are pursued".
n.4: To give the hand means to submit, or to make a treaty.
n.6: Or "by their hand", that is, by the enemy.
n.9: Or "For you have utterly rejected us; you are angry with us beyond measure", or "Or have you utterly rejected us? Are you angry with us beyond measure?" When the book is read aloud in the synagogue, verse 21 is repeated after this verse, so that the reading does not end on this note.
